title: Friction map + micro-journey heuristics — proto notes
content:
Context / intent:
I want a compact reference for how different in-product frictions (setup, prompts, cost warnings, latency) map to micro-journey heuristics we can surface and automate in the hosted API console and client SDKs. This is a personal proto-pad: half mapping, half rough PRD seeds, half experiment parking lot.

Problem statement (single line):
Users give up or overpay when they mis-estimate token cost and latency for a given feature; we should reduce cognitive load and make better defaults / fallbacks that preserve utility while keeping unit economics predictable.

Top-level ideas (sketch):
- Friction types: onboarding (key/region config), prompt tuning (long instructions), session growth (context bloat), cost surprise (unexpected tokens), latency spikes (model switch needed), privacy gating (private deploy requirement).
- Heuristic responses: inline cost estimate, graded fidelity presets (low/med/high), preflight sampling (one-shot cheap check), auto-trim suggestions (compressor hint UI), graceful degrade pipeline (reduce depth -> switch quantized model -> partial streaming).

Mini PRD seeds:
Goal: Add a "Friction Advisor" surface in the Console + JS SDK that: (1) surfaces predicted token cost & latency for example prompts, (2) suggests 1–2 lower-cost alternatives and (3) tracks user acceptance so suggestions improve.
Key metrics: adoption (click-through on suggestions), cost delta (tokens/customer-hour), retention on trial flows, time-to-first-successful-gen.
Assumptions: server can cheaply sample prompt with a short-ctx subset; we have telemetry for tokens-per-call and model-latency distribution.

User stories (rough):
- As a frontend engineer onboarding Redwood, I want to see an estimated per-request cost for my sample prompt so I can pick the right default model.
- As a PM running a trial, I want a list of suggested prompt trims and a preview of expected output so I can lower cost without losing utility.
- As a Platform engineer, I want the SDK to fallback to a quantized variant automatically when latency exceeds 95th percentile for a given route.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console: sample input box + cost/latency estimate for 3 candidate models (fast/standard/cheap).
- SDK: API to request estimate + opt-in auto-fallback policy that can be enabled per-route.
- Telemetry: suggestion_shown, suggestion_accepted, fallback_triggered events with metadata (route_id, model_variant, cost_estimate, actual_tokens).

Open questions / risks:
- Sampling bias: estimating on short prefix may undercount final tokens (streamed generation breadth). Need heuristics for multiplier or sample-run.
- Privacy: sampling customer prompts in hosted product — need opt-in or local-simulate mode.
- Cost of sampling: we will spend tokens to estimate tokens — ROI analysis needed.

Experiment ideas (quick A/B):
A: show suggestion only in Console -> measure adoption of lower-cost models.
B: show suggestion in SDK (client-side) as preflight -> measure reduction in trial spend.
C: autopilot fallback after N slow responses -> measure error rate changes.

Implementation sketch (rough tech notes):
- Step 1 (Console): UI with 3 model suggestions + deterministic token estimate using tokenization lib and cached per-model per-seq multipliers.
- Step 2 (SDK): expose estimateTokenCost(prompt, options) returning {estimated_tokens, estimated_ms, model_rank}. Keep offline deterministic version to avoid sampling cost; add sample-run as optional.
- Step 3: telemetry hooks + lightweight ML model to learn multiplier per-route over time (ML in Optimize later).

Telemetry / schema (proto-level):
- suggestion_shown: {route, user_tier, model_choices, est_tokens, est_latency}
- suggestion_choice: {route, chosen_model, est_tokens, act_tokens, delta_tokens}
- fallback_triggered: {route, orig_model, fallback_model, reason(latency|cost|error), act_latency}

Notes to self / quick todo list:
- Talk to infra about cheap sampling quota (JIRA INF-1293).
- Sketch Console surface with Maya + design (quick wire in Figma).
- Draft SDK API signature and backwards-compat notes (no blocking for existing clients).
- Add privacy opt-out toggle for sampling / store only aggregates.

Parking lot (later):
- Per-customer calibrated multipliers (learned post-deploy).
- Inline small-editor that suggests prompt fixes (like remove/shorten instruction blocks).
- Automatic rollouts: candidate fallback policies that degrade quality gracefully with canary.%

Quick mental models / heuristics (for product conversations):
- "1 token tax" rule: short instructions often cause huge variance; display reasonable range not point-estimate.
- Prioritize UX for first-run flows: a single clear suggestion beats multiple nuanced ones.
- Cost-safety defaults: for 'trial' accounts use cheaper model default + visible button to 'upgrade fidelity'.

Useful links / refs (scratch):
- CON-4821 Journey canvas (internal, design).
- INF-1293 sampling quota thread (Jira).
- slack #console-ui thread: "preflight-estimates" (link pinned).
- PR link for tokenization lib update: github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizer-plus PR #12

Closing note:
This doc is a working thoughtpad — it intentionally mixes UX, metrics, and infra constraints. Next step: convert to a minimal 1‑page PRD for review with Maya and put a spike ticket for deterministic estimator (no sample-run).
